To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of the AcrA-TolC complex in the resting state shows that TolC is in an open conformation, that the structure of AcrAB-TollC complex in the transport state shows that Tolc is in a closed conformation, and that the structure of a complex of AcrA and AcrB with TolC in an intermediate conformation shows that TolC has a partially open conformation.

The AcrAB-T olC pump, a prototypical bacterial multidrug transporter, undergoes a large quaternary structural rearrangement to open the channel for drug transport, and that the channel remains open during the entire transport cycle.
The cryo-EM structure of the AcrA-AcrB-TolC complex revealed a quaternary switch that allosteric couples the drug binding to the channel opening.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function, regulation, and assembly of the AcrA/B/TolC multidrug pump.
the molecular mechanism of the AcrB efflux transporter, which is a key component in bacterial drug resistance.
the molecular mechanisms of bacterial drug export systems, and the role these systems play in antibiotic resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AcrAB–TolC pump uses an allosteric mechanism to couple ligand binding to the opening of the TolC channel.
AcrAB-TOLC is an allosteric pump.

the AcrAB pump is a highly complex and dynamic system, which is capable of responding to a variety of stimuli and environmental cues to achieve a high level of flexibility and efficiency, which is required for the pump to function properly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have determined the structures of the AcrB-TolC complex at near-atomic resolution in both the drug-free resting state and the transport state with a bound substrate.
we have solved the structure of the AcrB pump in the absence and presence of drug, and we have also solved the structure of a drug-bound AcrAB-Toc complex.
the AcrAB pump uses a novel allosteric mechanism to couple substrate recognition with channel opening, and that the AcrB homodimer is the functional unit for drug recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to capture the AcrAB TolC pump in a state where it was transporting a molecule of the antibiotic ciprofloxacin.
the AcrAB–TolC multidrug pump undergoes a large conformational rearrangement upon drug binding.
the AcrAB efflux pump is a dynamic machine, and the structures we determined show how it works.
